front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The name of this Surah is composed of two words, Ha-Mim and As-Sajdah, which implies that it is a Surah that begins with Ha-Mim and one that requires the performance of sajdah tilawah (prostration) that occurs in Ayat 38.
FYI – Not to be confused with Surah 32 As Sajdah.
This Surah is also called Fussilat. (Ayat 3 & 44) Fussilate is derived from the word tafseer that means to explain.

items.text: كِتٰبٌ فُصِّلَتۡ اٰيٰتُهٗ قُرۡاٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِّقَوۡمٍ يَّعۡلَمُوۡنَۙ
(41:3) a Book whose verses are perfectly explained—a Quran in Arabic for people who understand

وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنٰهُ قُرۡاٰنًا اَعۡجَمِيًّا لَّقَالُوۡا لَوۡلَا فُصِّلَتۡ اٰيٰتُهٗ ؕ ءَؔاَعۡجَمِىٌّ وَّعَرَبِىٌّ  ؕ قُلۡ هُوَ لِلَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ  ؕ وَ الَّذِيۡنَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُوۡنَ فِىۡۤ اٰذَانِهِمۡ وَقۡرٌ وَّهُوَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ عَمًى ؕ اُولٰٓـئِكَ يُنَادَوۡنَ مِنۡ مَّكَانٍۢ بَعِيۡدٍ

(41:44) Had We revealed this as a non-Arabic Quran they would have said: “Why were its verses not clearly explained? How strange, a non-Arabic scripture and an Arab audience!” Tell them: “It is a guidance and a healing to the believers. But to those who do not believe, it serves as a plug in their ears and a covering over their eyes. It is as if they are being called from a place far away.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah. This Surah has 54 Ayats in 6 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
There are seven Surahs in the Quran that begin with HaMim and they are:  (i) al-Momin (40), (ii) HaMim al-Sajdah (41) (iii) Ash-Shura (42), (iv) al-Zukhruf (43), (v) al-Dukhan (44) , (vi) al-Jathiyah (45), (vii) al-Ahqaf (46). These seven Surahs are also called "al-Hawamim". They are all Makki Surahs and were revealed one after another. The central theme is Tawhid. These are Surahs of Da'wah, inviting people to the EXCLUSIVE belief in Allah SWT.
The final authority regarding the significance and meaning of these disjointed Arabic letters (HaMim) in the beginning of each Surah is Allah AWT Himself.
The subject matter of this HaMim Surah is Tuahid and also Dawah. That is, once our own belief in Tawhid becomes firm then it is our duty to ensure that others are also enlighten with the gift of faith so from individual now, we focus on the community/society. In this Surah the Quran is mentioned in 16 places because the medium for Dawah is the Quran.
The unbelieving Quraysh gave a clear warning to the Holy Prophet that, "You may continue your mission of inviting people to Islam but we will go on opposing you as hard as we can so as to frustrate your mission."

items.text: (41:5) They say, “Our hearts are veiled against what you are calling us to, there is deafness in our ears, and there is a barrier between us and you. So do ˹whatever you want˺ and so shall we!”

So, whenever the Holy Prophet or a follower of his would try to recite the Quran before the people, they would at once raise such a hue and cry that no one could hear anything. The disbelievers would also isolate words and sentences of the Quran and then add their own words in order to distort the meaning and create misunderstanding among the people about the Quran and the Messenger who presented it.
Allah SWT addresses such people in Ayat 40:

(41:40) Those who distort the meaning of Our message are not hidden from Us. Is he who is hurled into the Fire better, or he who comes through safely on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you want, God certainly sees everything you do.
Allah SWT has taken the responsibility of persevering the Quran so no one can change or distort the Mighty Book. And a great punishment awaits those who try.

sections.title: 1-8 AL-QURAN IS A GIVER OF GOOD NEWS AND ADMONITION AND WOE TO THOSE WHO DENY THE HEREAFTER AND DO NOT PAY ZAKAH

arabic_lines: حٰمٓ ۚ

translation.text: Ha'. Mim

arabic_lines: تَنۡزِيۡلٌ مِّنَ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِۚ

translation.text: This is a revelation from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate,

arabic_lines: كِتٰبٌ فُصِّلَتۡ اٰيٰتُهٗ قُرۡاٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِّقَوۡمٍ يَّعۡلَمُوۡنَۙ

translation.text: a Book whose verses are perfectly explained—a Quran in Arabic for people who understand

commentary.text: Also called Surah Fussilat (above). Fassala means to break things up so that each part is separated from the next so that we deal with them one matter one at a time so that there is no ambiguity. And thus are the Surahs in the Quran.

translation.text: delivering good news and warning. Yet most of them turn away, so they do not hear.

commentary.text: Description of the Qur'an, and what Those Who turn away from it say
Below is a brief introduction to Ayat 1 – 4:

The first thing said is that this Word is a revelation from God, Lord of the worlds. If you reject it, you reject Allah’s Word, not a man’s word. And if you turn away from it, you do not turn away from a man but from Allah SWT.

Secondly, that God (the sender of this revelation) is extremely Merciful (Rehman and Rahim) to His creatures. The mention of the attribute of mercy, instead of any other attribute, points to the truth that

Indeed, the Quran is a supreme blessing sent down for the guidance and well-being of mankind. If God were merciless to mankind, He would have left us to wander about in darkness without guidance or any laws/rules etc.

Thirdly, there is nothing confusing and/or ambiguous in the Quran that hinders understanding. It has been explained plainly as to what constitutes success and what leads to failure, what are the right beliefs and what are the wrong beliefs, what is good and what is evil, what is high morality and what is vice, in what way lies the good of man and in what he incurs loss for himself.

كِتٰبٌ فُصِّلَتۡ Fussilate: Means to separate in sections so as to make the meaning clear and distinct. Fussilate is derived from the word tafseer means to explain. The Quran is clear and detailed in its meaning and sound and wise in its rulings. Thus, the Quran is not a book of riddles, poetry, or conjecture with hidden meanings rather a clear Book of guidance/mercy/good news and warning.

Fourthly, that this is an Arabic Quran, that is if this Quran had been sent down in some other language, the Arabs would have presented the excuse that they were ignorant of the language in which God had sent His Book. But this is their language.

Fifthly, that this Book is for those who possess knowledge. That is, only the people of understanding can draw any benefit from this Book. For the ignorant it is as useless as a precious diamond for the one who cannot distinguish it from a mere stone.
Sixthly, that this Book gives good news and administers warning. There is a wonderful balance between the two, good news and warning. One is not mentioned without the other.

Lesson: True knowledge is the correct understanding of the Quran. For every Muslim it is imperative to gain this knowledge before or at the very least in conjunction with wordily knowledge. Make Quran your priority.

arabic_lines: قُلۡ اِنَّمَاۤ اَنَا بَشَرٌ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يُوۡحٰٓى اِلَىَّ اَنَّمَاۤ اِلٰهُكُمۡ اِلٰـهٌ وَّاحِدٌ فَاسۡتَقِيۡمُوۡۤا اِلَيۡهِ وَاسۡتَغۡفِرُوۡهُ ؕ وَوَيۡلٌ لِّلۡمُشۡرِكِيۡنَ ۙ

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a man like you, ˹but˺ it has been revealed to me that your God is only One God. So take the Straight Way towards Him, and seek His forgiveness. Woe to those who associate others with Allah in His Divinity,

commentary.text: The Call to Tawhid
Invoke and worship only Allah SWT Who is the One and only God. Do not commit shirk by bowing down to others for help and do not obey and follow the customs, laws and codes set by others.

فَاسْتَقِيمُوا إِلَيْهِ So take the Straight Way towards Him…Here we find the stress on doing ones best in the way of Islam as opposed to a weak, half-hearted effort. Strive with full conviction & steadfastness in the way of the truth.

Lesson: Don’t waste all your striving and energy for worldly endeavors i.e studies, career, family, homes etc. Give the Quran its right which is that it should be (i) recited in Arabic (ii) understood and then (iii) obeyed.

translation.text: who do not pay Zakat, and who deny the Hereafter.

commentary.text: The word Zakat here is used for purity (in its linguistic form). The law for payment of zakat was first revealed in Madina and this is a Makki Surah. Thus, here zakat means the purity of the soul that ensues from belief in Tawhid, the Hereafter and obedience to Allah SWT. According to this explanation the translation of the Ayat would be: Woe to the mushriks, who do not adopt purity.

translation.text: As to those who have faith and do good works, surely theirs shall be a never-ending reward.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + Good/Righteous deeds = Success
Lesson: The reward for being steadfast in faith and preforming righteous deeds will be endless and continuous blessings in the Hereafter.

sections.title: 9-12 STORY OF THE CREATION OF EARTH, MOUNTAINS, SEASONS, SKIES AND HEAVENS

translation.text: Tell them, (O Prophet): “Do you indeed disbelieve in Him and assign compeers to Him Who created the earth in two days? He is the Lord of all beings of the Universe.
(After creating the earth) He set up firm mountains on it, blessed it, and provided it with sustenance in proportion to the needs of all who seek (sustenance). All this was done in four days.

commentary.text: Some Details of the Creation of this Universe

The creation of the earth took two days and the setting up of the mountains and placing of the provisions and blessings in it took two days, then the creation of the heavens, as mentioned below, took another two days, thus, the total number of the days is six.
Also see (Surah Al- Aaraf, Ayat 54); (Surah Younus, Ayat 3), (Surah Houd, Ayat 7); (Surah Al-Furqan, Ayat 59).
(41:9 and 10) These are from the Ayat Mutashabih

Some ayats in the Quran are decisive (Muhkam), they are the basis of the Book, and others are allegorical (Mutashabih); then as for those in whose hearts there is perversity they follow the part of it which is allegorical, seeking to mislead and seeking to give it (their own) interpretation but none knows its interpretation except Allah. Conversely, those who are firmly rooted in knowledge say: We believe in it, it is all from our Lord.

sections.title: 13-18 WARNING TO THE DISBELIEVERS AND THE EXAMPLE OF ALLAH'S SCOURGE UPON THE NATIONS OF AD AND THAMUD

translation.text: But if they turn away, tell them: “I warn you against a sudden scourge like that which struck Ad and Thamud.”

commentary.text: A Warning to the Disbelievers and a Reminder of the Story of Ad and Thamud

If they (mushirk) disbelieve in Tawhid (which means Allah SWT is the One and only One, Who has created this earth and the whole universe) and if they persist in associating others as their deities beside Him (commit shirk), then here is a warning for them: 'beware of incurring the same fate as Ad and Thamud.'

translation.text: As for Ad, they acted arrogantly throughout the land with no right, boasting, “Who is superior to us in might?” Did they not see that Allah Himself, Who created them, was far superior to them in might? Still they persisted in denying Our signs.

So We sent against them a furious wind, for several miserable days, to make them taste a humiliating punishment in this worldly life. But far more humiliating will be the punishment of the Hereafter. And they will not be helped.

commentary.text: The details of this torment given in other places of the Quran show that an intense/severe/loud wind storm continued to rage for seven nights and eight days consecutively. It swept people off the ground and they fell down dead, scattered like hollow trunks of the palm-tree. (Surah Al- Haaqqah, Ayat 7). It left rotting everything on which it blew. (Surah Adh-Dhariyat, Ayat 42). The remnants of their population was humbled and debased before the very nations they used to intimidate by their show of power and might.

This humiliating torment was sent due to the arrogance the people of Ad had assumed in the land without any right, boasting that there was none more powerful than them on earth. They denied despite knowing the truth – preferring to remain in ignorance. Thus, Allah SWT disgraced and destroyed them in this world and an even worse outcome awaits them in the Hereafter.
For details of the story of Ad see (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 65-72); (Surah Houd, Ayats 50-60); (Surah Al-Muminun, Ayats 32-41); (Surah Ash- Shuara, Ayats 123-140); (Surah Al-Ankabut, Ayat 40)

translation.text: As for Thamud, We bestowed guidance upon them, but they preferred to remain blind rather than be guided. At last a humiliating scourge overtook them on account of their misdeeds.
Yet We delivered those who believed and were God-fearing.

commentary.text: The Prophets and their followers were saved. The above Ayats exemplify the balance between issuing warnings (41:13 – 41:17) followed by good news (41:18). The outcome of the believers and disbelievers is never the same.
Lesson: Arrogance leads to destruction.

sections.title: 19-25 ON THE DAY OF JUDGMENT PEOPLE'S OWN EARS, EYES AND SKINS WILL BEAR WITNESS AGAINST THEM RELATING TO THEIR MISDEEDS

translation.text: Consider the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered for the Fire, all driven in ranks.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgment, the court will start its work only when all former and later generations have assembled together in the Plain of Resurrection. (For further explanation, see (Surah Al-Aaraf, 38-39).

Whatever a person does in his lifetime, whether good or evil, its influence and impact continues long after his death -- for which he is totally responsible. Similarly, earlier generations continue to influence/affect later generations for centuries and are responsible for their heritage.
Lesson: What will your legacy be?

translation.text: and when all have arrived, their ears, their eyes, and their skins shall bear witness against them, stating all that they had done in the life of the world.

commentary.text: When a stubborn culprit persists in denying his crimes, then the limbs of his body will bear witness and speak against him regarding the offenses he committed through them.

translation.text: Yet you did not try to hide yourselves from your ears, eyes, and skin to prevent them from testifying against you. You thought that God did not know about much of what you were doing,

commentary.text: When you secretly committed sins you never thought that your ears, eyes or your skin would ever bear witness or speak against you rather you thought that Allah SWT does not even know what you do.

arabic_lines: وَذٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ الَّذِىۡ ظَنَنۡتُمۡ بِرَبِّكُمۡ اَرۡدٰٮكُمۡ فَاَصۡبَحۡتُمۡ مِّنَ الۡخٰسِرِيۡن

translation.text: It was that false assumption you entertained about your Lord that has brought about your doom, so you have become losers.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF LOSERS

Here we find the definition of FAILURE!  A person who is not knowledgeable about his Lord and finds complacency in ignorance. For example, if you sin and then presume that Allah SWT will not punish you because you are of a certain lineage then that false assumption is wrong and will potentially lead you to sin more. However, if you realize that Allah SWT is merciful but also severe in retribution one is careful to never sin.
Prophet (PBUH) expressed thus: Your Lord says: 'I am as my servant thinks I am.' (Bukhari, Muslim)

Hasan Basri has explained this Ayat thus: Every man’s attitude and conduct is determined by the thought and supposition that he holds about his Lord. The conduct of a righteous believer is right because his thought and assumption about his Lord is right and the conduct of a disbeliever is wrong because his thought and conjecture about his Lord is wrong.
Lesson: Don’t make baseless assumptions and have false expectations about Allah SWT. Gain knowledge and reflect.

arabic_lines: وَقَيَّضۡنَا لَهُمۡ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُوۡا لَهُمۡ مَّا بَيۡنَ اَيۡدِيۡهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ الۡقَوۡلُ فِىۡۤ اُمَمٍ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِنۡ قَبۡلِهِمۡ مِّنَ الۡجِنِّ وَالۡاِنۡسِۚ اِنَّهُمۡ كَانُوۡا خٰسِرِيۡنَ

translation.text: We have appointed, for the disbelievers, companions who make their past and present seem fair and right to them, but the sentence has already been passed on them, along with generations of jinn and men before them: they were losers.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF LOSERS
Here again we find the definition of a LOSER!

The law of nature dictates that man inclines towards those with similar thinking and attitudes. If a wicked person happens to be associated with a good individual, he/she cannot remain associated with him/her for long. Likewise, if good and noble man happens to be associated with evil intentioned and immoral men their association cannot last long.
……who make their past and present seem fair and right to them……

The companions/friends of disbelievers tend to beautify their sins for them by assuring them that their past has been glorious and their future will also be bright. They portray evil as attractive asserting that there is no Hereafter where one might be called to account for ones deeds. If at all, the Hereafter does exist then God who has blessed them in the world will bless them there too.
……but the sentence has already been passed on them, along with generations of jinn and men before them: they were losers……
Allah SWT tells us that He appoints, for those who continue to deny, close companions from among the devils of men and Jinn. And these people are the losers.
In Surah Az Zukhruf, Ayat 36 & 37, Allah SWT says:

And whosoever turns away blindly from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, We appoint for him a Shaytan to be a companion for him. And verily, they hinder them from the path, but they think that they are guided aright! (43:36-37)
Lesson: Surround yourself with pious/good people who do not make sin attractive or feel inconsequential. This will be of benefit in this world and the next.
Beware of company that beautifies sin thus making sin seem inconsequential and unimportant.

sections.title: 26-32 THOSE WHO DO NOT LISTEN TO AL-QURAN SHALL BE STERNLY PUNISHED AND THOSE WHO DO NOT LISTEN TO THOSE WHO SAY OUR GOD IS ALLAH AND THEN STAY FIRM ON IT, ANGELS ARE ASSIGNED FOR THEIR PROTECTION

translation.text: The disbelievers say, ‘Do not listen to this Quran; drown it in frivolous talk: thus perhaps you may gain the upper hand.

commentary.text: The majesty of the Quran is mentioned here. To read, understand, recite and teach the Quran is something that satan dislikes very much. So anytime the Quran is understood and appreciated by people satan comes into immediate action – which is why institutions like Al-Huda are looked upon with such disdain and suspicion.

The disbelievers of Makkah wanted to frustrate the Prophet (PBUH)'s mission so whenever he would start reciting the Quran, they should create noise, clap hands, pass taunting remarks and raise all sorts of objections to subdue his voice. Thus, they hoped to defeat the Prophet of Allah.

translation.text: So We will certainly make the disbelievers taste a severe punishment, and We will surely repay them according to the worst of their deeds.
That is the reward of Allah’s enemies: the Fire, which will be their eternal home—a fitting reward for their denial of Our revelations.

commentary.text: Here the anger of Allah SWT becomes apparent for those who reject the QURAN. Never be someone who mocks, ridicules or tries of defeat or distort the message of Allah SWT as then you will become an enemy of Allah SWT. (May Allah SWT protect us all). Hell is the reward for the enemies of Allah SWT.
Lesson: When discussing religion or Allah SWT be exceedingly cautious with your words and attitude, approaching the subject with the humility, due reverence, honesty and knowledge that is it's due.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ الَّذِيۡنَ قَالُوۡا رَبُّنَا اللّٰهُ ثُمَّ اسۡتَقَامُوۡا تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيۡهِمُ الۡمَلٰٓـئِكَةُ اَلَّا تَخَافُوۡا وَلَا تَحۡزَنُوۡا وَاَبۡشِرُوۡا بِالۡجَـنَّةِ الَّتِىۡ كُنۡتُمۡ تُوۡعَدُوۡنَ

translation.text: Those who say “Allah is our Lord” and then remain steadfast, upon them descend angels (and say): “Do not fear nor grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise which you were promised.

commentary.text: Glad Tidings to Those Who believe in Allah Alone and stand firm

After warning the disbelievers regarding the consequences of their opposition to the truth which is a permanent residence in hell (41:28), now the address turns to the believers and the Prophet (PBUH). That is, those who embraced their faith sincerely and steadfastly, fulfilling the demands of the doctrine of Tawhid.

This Ayat is the pinnacle/essence of Iman as well as the central Ayat of this Surah: (i) Declare the oneness of Allah SWT and then (ii) Then remain steadfast ثُمَّ اسۡتَقَامُوۡا upon this conviction no matter what the situation or circumstance. Even in the darkest and toughest of times you do not dare hold any grudge against your Raab rather are patient, grateful and worship Allah SWT understanding that He is the one who provides sustenance, offers relief, heals the sick, etc. Thus, rely only and solely upon the Raab of the Universe.
…..upon them descend angels (and say): “Do not fear nor grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise which you were promised……

Angels come to receive believers at the time of death, welcome them in the grave (in the state of barzakh), and accompany them on the Day of Resurrection, yet, their (angles) company is not restricted to the Hereafter but remains available in this world too. Angels are the companions or wail (guardians) for believers both in this world and the next – bringing peace and tranquility to the beliver.
Hadith: Whoever sits on the prayer mat after salah doing zikr then angles continue pray for his/her forgiveness until they get up or break wuzu.

Lesson: Steadfastness اسۡتَقَامُوۡ (istaqama) more often than not leads to loneliness because one is leaving many things behind including bad company. But remember Allah SWT never leaves such a person alone – Allah SWT guides and aids/protects such a person and so do the angels.

sections.title: 33-44 THE BEST IN SPEECH IS THE ONE WHO CALLS PEOPLE TOWARDS ALLAH, DO GOOD DEEDS AND SAY, "I AM A MUSLIM". EXAMPLE OF ALLAH'S SIGNS AND NOTHING IS SAID TO MUHAMMAD WHICH WAS NOT SAID TO THE PRIOR PROPHETS AND AL-QURAN IS A GUIDE AND HEALING FOR THE BELIEVERS

translation.text: And who is fairer in speech than he who calls to Allah and acts righteously and says: “I am a Muslim”?

commentary.text: The Virtue of calling Others to Allah SWT
After reassuring and encouraging believers, we are now counseled as to our real duty in life.
In the preceding Ayats we are told: (i) Be firm/steadfast in the service and submission to Allah SWT as it is that which makes man a friend of the angels and worthy of Paradise. (Tawhid)

Now we are being told: (ii) The next thing which wins man the highest place of honor is that he/she lead by example in performing good deeds and also invite others to the worship of Allah SWT. (Dawah)

arabic_lines: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِى الۡحَسَنَةُ وَ لَا السَّيِّئَةُ ؕ اِدۡفَعۡ بِالَّتِىۡ هِىَ اَحۡسَنُ فَاِذَا الَّذِىۡ بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهٗ عَدَاوَةٌ كَاَنَّهٗ وَلِىٌّ حَمِيۡمٌ

translation.text: (O Prophet), good and evil are not equal. Repel (evil) with that which is good, and you will see that he, between whom and you there was enmity, shall become as if he were a bosom friend (of yours).

commentary.text: Wisdom in Dawah

In very discouraging times and conditions when apparently every way of extending an invitation to Islam seemed to be blocked, the Prophet (PBUH) was taught this formula for inviting people to Islam. (Dawah)

Firstly, know that goodness and evil are not equal, as if to say: Although apparently your opponents might have raised a dreadful storm of mischief and evil, against which goodness seems absolutely helpless and powerless, yet, evil in itself has a weakness which ultimately causes its own destruction. For as long as man is man, his nature cannot help hating evil.

Secondly, know that evil should be resisted not by mere goodness but by a superior good, as if to say: If a person treats you unjustly and you forgive him, then it is mere good. The superior good is that you treat the one who ill-treats you with kindness and love. The result will be that your worst enemy becomes your closest friend, (as this is human nature.)
Lesson: The best dawah is to kill them with kindness.

translation.text: But none attains to this except those who are steadfast; none attains to this except those endowed with mighty good fortune.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS

A man may instinctively act benevolently, in response, to an evil done and there is nothing extraordinary in it. However, when a person has to fight/strive for years, for the sake of truth, it requires an extraordinary amount of patience and humility to go on resisting evil with good, and that too with the superior good.
Steadfastness, patience, and humility in faith lead to a Mighty Good Fortune.

translation.text: And if you are prompted by a provocation from Satan, seek refuge with Allah. He, and He alone, is All-Hearing, All- Knowing.

commentary.text: Be on your guard against the provocations of Satan. He will incite you as a well-wisher and sincere friend. Whenever you feel an undue poking, seek Allah’s refuge by reciting the Taawwuz.
AUZUBILLAH MINASHAITAN NIRAJEEM
The meaning is “I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Shaitan."
Al-Nahl  (16:98) So, when you recite the Qurān, seek refuge with Allah against Satan, the accursed.

Imam Ahmad has related on the authority of Abu Hurairah that once a man started uttering abuses against Abu Bakr in the presence of the Prophet (PBUH). Abu Bakr kept on hearing the attacks quietly and the Prophet (PBUH) kept on smiling at them. At last, when Abu Bakr could restrain himself any longer, he also uttered a harsh word to the person in response. No sooner did he utter the word, that the Prophet (PBUH) rose and left the place immediately. Abu Bakr followed him and asked: How is it that as long as the person went on abusing me, you kept quiet and smiling but when I said a word in retaliation, you were annoyed. The Prophet (PBUH) replied: As long as you were quiet, an angel remained with you who went on replying to him on your behalf but when you spoke out, Satan came in place of the angel. I could not sit with Satan.

What brings patience, peace and tranquility to the heart of the believer is the conviction that Allah SWT is not unaware. He knows whatever we are doing as well as that which is being done against us. He is hearing and watching the conduct of both parties. On this very conviction, the believer entrusts his own and the opponents of the truth’s affair to Allah SWT and remains satisfied.

This is the fifth place where the Prophet, and through him, the believers have been taught this wisdom of preaching and reforming the people. For the other four places, see (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 199-204), (Surah An-Nahl, Ayats 125- 128), (Surah Al-Muminun, Ayats 96-98), (Surah Al-Ankabut, Ayats 46-47)

translation.text: And of His Signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate yourselves before the sun, nor before the moon, but prostrate yourselves before Allah Who created them, if it is Him that you serve.

commentary.text: Man is told not to commit shirk by associating others in the worship and submission of Allah SWT. Embrace Tawhid fully and completely.

The polytheists excuse for worshipping the sun and the moon was that they did not bow to these objects but bowed to God through them. An answer to this has been given here, so as to say: There is no need for any intermediaries, bow down to Allah SWT directly?

translation.text: But if they are too proud, then let them know that those ˹angels˺ nearest to your Lord glorify Him day and night, and never grow weary.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says that if some are too arrogant to bow down to their Creator, no worries, as legions upon legions of angels, willingly and happily, testify every moment that their Lord is pure and exalted. So be of those who prostrate willing and happily to Allah SWT.
Lesson: Ironically, we happily submit/humble to ourselves to society, our jobs etc. (the creation of Allah SWT), yet, are too proud to prorate to the Creator.
IT IS OBLIGATORY TO PERFORM SAJDAH TILAWAT (PROSTRATION) HERE.
Lesson: Be of those who prostrate happily, with humility and never weary of submitting to Allah SWT – for our well-being in the world and the next depends upon it.

translation.text: These are the ones who rejected the Good Counsel when it came to them, although it is certainly a Mighty Book.

commentary.text: Description of the Quran
Allah SWT describes the Quran as a mighty, honorable, dominant Book. A Book that has been preserved and protected by Allah SWT Himself.
Important to note that the consequence of those who reject the Quran has not been mentioned above suggesting that the outcome of such an action is too grave to even state.
Quran is also referred to as 'zikr' or reminder. This fortifies the principle in religion that this message is part of our fitra (nature) and contains nothing new in it rather is just a reminder.
Lesson: Recite the Quran (in Arabic). Make Quran a priority.

translation.text: Falsehood may not enter it from the front or from the rear. It is a revelation that has been sent down from the Most Wise, the Immensely Praiseworthy.

commentary.text: None have succeed in proving any teaching or statement in the Quran as false either by making a frontal attack on it nor 'from the rear' means that nothing can be discovered till Resurrection which may be opposed to the truths and realities presented by the Quran; that is no new science, no new experiment or observation can be made to prove that the guidance given to man by the Quran, whether it be in respect to beliefs, morality, laws, civilization, economics, society, politics, biology, chemistry, etc. is wrong/false.

That which this Book has declared as the truth can never be proven to be falsehood and that which it has declared as falsehood can never be proven to be the truth.  The wisdom of this Book is eternal.
Lesson: Read the Quran will full confidence that it contains only the truth.

arabic_lines: وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنٰهُ قُرۡاٰنًا اَعۡجَمِيًّا لَّقَالُوۡا لَوۡلَا فُصِّلَتۡ اٰيٰتُهٗ ؕ ءَؔاَعۡجَمِىٌّ وَّعَرَبِىٌّ  ؕ قُلۡ هُوَ لِلَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ  ؕ وَ الَّذِيۡنَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُوۡنَ فِىۡۤ اٰذَانِهِمۡ وَقۡرٌ وَّهُوَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ عَمًى ؕ اُولٰٓـئِكَ يُنَادَوۡنَ مِنۡ مَّكَانٍۢ بَعِيۡد

translation.text: Had We revealed this as a non-Arabic Quran they would have said: “Why were its verses not clearly explained? How strange, a non-Arabic scripture and an Arab audience!” Tell them: “It is a guidance and a healing to the believers. But to those who do not believe, it serves as a plug in their ears and a covering over their eyes. It is as if they are being called from a place far away.

commentary.text: Rejection or disbelief of the Quran is pure Obstinacy

The disbelievers said: Muhammad (PBUH) is an Arab. Arabic is his mother tongue. How can one believe that the Arabic Quran he presents has not been forged by him. The Quran could be believed to be the revelation of God if he, Muhammad (PBUH), had started speaking fluently in a foreign language.

Their argument is being refuted by Allah SWT: 'Now when the Quran has been sent down in their own tongue so that they may understand it, they raise the objection of why it been sent down to an Arab in Arabic? But if it had been sent down in a foreign tongue, these very people would have said: How strange!' An Arab Messenger has been sent to the Arabs, but the revelations being sent to him are in a tongue that is neither understood by him nor by his people.
Here again the word "Fussilate" is used.
وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنٰهُ قُرۡاٰنًا اَعۡجَمِيًّا لَّقَالُوۡا لَوۡلَا فُصِّلَتۡ اٰيٰتُهٗ
……Tell them: “It is a guidance and a healing to the believers…….

Allah SWT says the Quran is a Book that contains guidance and shifa (cure) but only for those who believe, as they are the ones who benefit. Those who disbelieve are cursed with a deafness and blindness that prevents them from seeing/hearing/benefiting from the Quran.

**Shifa or cure in the Quran means that by reciting the Quran in Arabic we can be cured of physical and spiritual aliments i.e. the Prophet would perform Rukya for physical illness as well as disease of the heart, such as, doubt, confusion, jealously towards others, hatred, depression, magic and the whispering of Satan etc.
…….But to those who do not believe, it serves as a plug in their ears and a covering over their eyes. It is as if they are being called from a place far away…..

This simile depicts the psychology of the stubborn opponents, that is, when a person is summoned from afar, he hears a voice but does not understand what is being said. Thus, in spite of hearing the Quran disbelievers will not understand.
Lesson: Those who do not want to understand the Quran will make all kinds of excuses. Focus dawah efforts mostly on those who are receptive to the message of Allah SWT.
Recite the Quran in Arabic for shifa or cure of the body and soul.

sections.title: 45-46 THE BOOK GIVEN TO PROPHET MUSA WAS SIMILAR TO AL-QURAN

translation.text: And in the past We gave Moses the Book and yet it became an object of dispute.  If your Lord's decree had not gone forth before, a decisive judgement would have been made among them, once and for all. Surely they are in a disquieting doubt about it.

commentary.text: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is being reassured that Prophet Musa (PBUH) was also given a Book (Torah). Some believed in the divine books while others made up their minds to oppose them.
If Allah SWT had not already decreed that all disputes would be decided on the Day of Judgment, then the reality would have been made clear as to who is in the right and who is in the wrong.
